Let P be its focus and \(d_{a}\) its directrix. The envelope of \(d_{a}\) as P moves on circumcircle is a circle, O_{a}. Define (O_{b}) and (O_{c}) cyclically. The radical center of the circles (O_{a}), (O_{b}), (O_{c}) is X_13419; see `Euclid #611 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/611>`__. (Angel Montesdeoca, February 6, 2020)

no: Suppose that P = \(p : q : r\) (barycentrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle ABC. The Kiepert image of P is introduced here as the point K(P) = 1/(c^2 p^2 q^2+2 c^2 p q^3+2 c^2 p q^2 r+(a^2-b^2+c^2) q^3 r-b^2 p^2 r^2-2 b^2 p q r^2+(-b^2+c^2) q^2 r^2-2 b^2 p r^3+(-a^2-b^2+c^2) q r^3) : : Let K be the Kiepert hyperbola of the cevian triangle A'B'C' of P. Let A'' be the point, other than A', in which K meets line BC, and define B'' and C'' cyclically. The lines AA'', BB'', CC'' concur in K(P). (Peter Moses, June 15, 2017; see also X_13610.)
